examples.knowledge_point: Solving for Unknowns By Computing a Quotient and Equating Real and Imaginary Parts
examples.worked_solution:
First, we divide both sides of the equation by $1+\textrm{i}$ to isolate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}3+5\text{i} & =(p+\text{i}q)(1+\text{i}) \\ \frac{3+5\text{i}}{1+\text{i}} & =p+\text{i}q\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to simplify the fraction on the left-hand side, we multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(3+5\text{i})(1-\text{i})}{(1+\text{i})(1-\text{i})} & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{3-3\text{i}+5\text{i}-5{\text{i}}^{2}}{{1}^{2}-{\text{i}}^{2}} & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{3+2\text{i}-5(-1)}{1-(-1)} & =p+\text{i}q \\ \frac{8+2\text{i}}{2} & =p+\text{i}q \\ 4+\text{i} & =p+\text{i}q\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can equate the real parts and the imaginary parts separately.

- Equating the real parts, we get $4=p.$

- Equating the imaginary parts, we get $1=q.$

Therefore, $p=4$ and $q=1.$

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we multiply both sides of the equation by $2\text{i}$ to get rid of the fraction and isolate the variables:

$$
\begin{aligned}-4+\text{i} & =\frac{p+\text{i}q}{2\text{i}} \\ (-4+\text{i})(2\text{i}) & =p+\text{i}q \\ -8\text{i}+2{\text{i}}^{2} & =p+\text{i}q \\ -2-8\text{i} & =p+\text{i}q\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can equate the real parts and the imaginary parts separately.

- Equating the real parts, we get

$$
-2=p.
$$

- Equating the imaginary parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & =q.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=-2$ and $q=-8.$
